facts.state_of_play: Nearly a week after the Nov. 3 midterms, in which Democrats won both houses of Congress, Trump questioned the results without evidence on Truth Social Monday, reviving voting-machine claims after saying he accepted the outcome and might deal with Democrats. The administration asked the Supreme Court to make California set aside about 20,000 mail-in ballots, and DOJ is appealing dismissal of an Alaska Senate election suit. Officials are also leaving: Civil Division head Brett Shumate resigned Monday, and WH deputy chief of staff Richard Walters resigned Friday, amid a wave of post-midterm departures as Stephen Miller becomes chief of staff. Trump also ordered DOJ on Saturday to investigate members of Congress who proposed impeaching AG Blanche. Blanche signaled on CNN Sunday that Democrats could be investigated, and Sen. Elissa Slotkin's lawyer warned him not to obey Trump's demand to investigate her. Congressional Republicans are in turmoil after losing at least 30 House seats: House and Senate GOP leadership elections are set for Tuesday. Ron Johnson and four allies want the Senate vote delayed, targeting John Thune, while John Barrasso is seeking another term as whip. The party turmoil extends to the RNC: Trump is reportedly threatening to cut off the committee unless it reelects his pick, chair Joe Gruters, after co-chair KC Crosbie launched a challenge. Separately, Trump on Monday blamed old technology and the Biden administration for last week's nationwide grounding of all planes.

facts.state_of_play: Stephen Miller took over as White House chief of staff on Monday, replacing Susie Wiles, after Republicans lost the House and Senate in the midterms. Trump, after initially signaling acceptance, has questioned the early vote numbers and ballot machines, and admitted deportation policy was 'too tough'. Jeffries, poised to be Speaker, says Democrats will focus on affordability and corruption, and a closed-door briefing on the Huang affair is scheduled. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after 33 years amid allegations of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Trump, before leaving Monday for a multi-day Asia swing with summits with Xi and Putin in China, says a Kim Jong Un meeting is possible and that Kim's presence is up to Xi. On Monday the administration said it is moving forward with an interim rule, fiercely debated internally, requiring licenses to export AI chips if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries, closing a remote-access loophole ahead of the China trip and curbing a data center business serving Chinese companies. Trump also says he would not mind reinstating Huang, sees no national security risk and doubts she was a spy. A 'Bring Jensen Back' petition has thousands of signatures and tech figures are lobbying for his return, but a CNBC source says Nvidia's board is not considering it and is focused on a national security investigation; the NYT reports some in the administration oppose his return, and officials are reportedly trading blame. A Friday FAA nationwide ground stop of over four hours disrupted over a million passengers; Trump blames old equipment, denies responsibility, praised Duffy and lashed out at NBC's Yamiche Alcindor; Mullin says no one will be fired. Michigan Democrats remain split over Haley Stevens endorsing Mike Rogers.
